evidence.evidence_sentence: SEC fines two advisors, alleging they lied about AI
The 2 companies, Delphia (USA) Inc. and Global Predictions Inc., agreed to pay $400,000 in total penalties.
The SEC has said in enforcement orders that the Toronto-based Delphia and San Francisco-based Global Predictions made misleading statements about their use of AI to clients and prospective clients.

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced settled charges against two investment advisers, Delphia (USA) Inc. and Global Predictions Inc., for making false and misleading statements about their purported use of artificial intelligence (AI).
The 2 companies, Delphia (USA) Inc. and Global Predictions Inc., agreed to pay $400,000 in total penalties.
An internet-based advisor that provides portfolio allocation recommendations, Global Predictions does not directly manage assets, the company told the SEC in a filing this month.

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced settled charges against two investment advisers, Delphia (USA) Inc. and Global Predictions Inc., for making false and misleading statements about their purported use of artificial intelligence (AI).
Delphia USA and Global Predictions were fined $225,000 and $175,000, respectively, the SEC announced in a press release Monday.
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has charged two financial advising firms with "making false and misleading statements about their purported use of artificial intelligence (AI)."
2 RIAs have settled with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over claims the firms made about their use of artificial intelligence.

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced settled charges against two investment advisers, Delphia (USA) Inc. and Global Predictions Inc., for making false and misleading statements about their purported use of artificial intelligence (AI).

2 investment advisers agreed to pay a total of $400,000 to settle charges by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) the firms each engaged in artificial intelligence (AI) misrepresentations that misled clients about how they were using the technology.

The firm was also charged with violating the Marketing Rule, which, among other things, prohibits a registered investment adviser from disseminating any advertisement that includes any untrue statement of material fact.

Without admitting or denying the SEC's findings, Delphia and Global Predictions consented to the entry of orders finding that they violated the Advisers Act and ordering them to be censured and to cease and desist from violating the charged provisions.
Delphia USA and Global Predictions were fined $225,000 and $175,000, respectively, the SEC announced in a press release Monday.

The Securities and Exchange Commission ordered the owner of Rimar Capital and a board member of its holding company to pay nearly $524,000 in penalties for defrauding investors with false and misleading statements about its use of artificial intelligence.

The former chief executive officer of closed AI recruitment startup Joonko faces up to 40 years in prison and the potential of penalties levied by the Securities and Exchange Commission for allegedly defrauding investors of more than $27 million.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) took action against a pair of student loan debt relief companies for allegedly deceiving borrowers.

After dismissing its lawsuit against the crypto exchange Coinbase in March, a second investigation into the exchange by the Securities and Exchange Commission has surfaced, according to a report from the New York Times.
